{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVMdNDs8AAAABbHXbwQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BnXy5zhEsgW4", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BnXy5", "number": 67, "title": "Use one multi-animation glTF per character, shorten model labels, and investigate Uka sleeve deformation", "body": "## Context and user-visible problems

The public [Uka / Gene Light demo](https://takahirox.github.io/mmd-gltf/) now offers Rest, a facial sample, Laugh and Apology (Issues #63/#65, merged PRs #64/#66). Three follow-up problems were reported:

1. **Selecting Laugh/Apology triggers a complete viewer/model reload.** Instead, put all available motions in **one glTF asset per character**, load the character **once**, and select/replay the embedded glTF animation without reloading the PMX, glTF, renderer, textures, camera or GPU geometry.
2. **Model selector labels are redundant:** `Uka comparison` and `Gene Light comparison` should be just **`Uka`** and **`Gene Light`**. The page already communicates that this is a comparison.
3. **Uka's sleeve/clothing appears not to follow the animated arms during Laugh/Apology in BOTH panes.** Investigate the cause, collect evidence at representative frames, and fix the actual missing deformation when feasible rather than assuming an issue with vertex skinning or replacing source motion.

**Workflow/ownership:** Task for the designated implementer. The Issue author must **not implement code, create a branch, or open a PR**. Preserve the current independently rendered PMX-vs-glTF comparison and original assets.

## Confirmed implementation facts

### Why motion switching currently reloads everything

- [`examples/main.ts`](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/examples/main.ts#L338-L349) handles a new clip ID by calling `replaceMotion(next, camera)`.
- [`examples/demo.ts`](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/examples/demo.ts) then calls `old.dispose()`, deletes the existing viewer and calls `show(demo,next,view)` again.
- That re-creates the `WebGPURenderer`, OrbitControls, PMX loaded by `MMDLoader`, Toon and PBR GLTFLoader scenes, plugins, `VMDPlayer`s, morph projections and GPU resources, even though only the motion changed.
- [`tools/prepare-uka.ts`](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/tools/prepare-uka.ts), [`tools/prepare-example.ts`](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/tools/prepare-example.ts) and [`tools/public-motion.ts`](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/tools/public-motion.ts) currently produce the facial animation as `uka/model.gltf` or `gene-light/model.glb`, **plus separate** `02_laugh.gltf` and `22_apology.gltf` files. The body files share static binary buffers, but the application nonetheless reconstructs the entire character on selection.
- [`ConversionOptions`](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/tools/pmx-to-gltf.ts#L30-L33) currently accepts only one `vmd?: Uint8Array` per invocation; this is a **converter API limitation**, not a glTF format limitation.
- **Promising existing multi-animation support:** [`tools/vmd-animation.ts`](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/tools/vmd-animation.ts) `addVMDAnimation` creates an animation on a `Document`, and `VMDWriter.records` is keyed by animation. [`MMDVMDPlugin`](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/packages/three-mmd-vmd/index.ts) loops over `json.animations`, enforces consistent rest transforms across multiple VMD payloads, and exposes a `VMDPlayer` for each via `getVMDPlayers(gltf)`. **Leverage and test this**; don't assume that merely concatenating glTF `animations[]` gives correct animation ownership or independent morph bindings.

### Uka sleeve: strong evidence this is *sleeve IK*, not bone append

The pinned Uka PMX [source inventory](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/docs/uka-inventory.json) shows **10 IK controllers**. Six are explicitly for sleeves:

| PMX bone index | IK controller | Effector bone index | Link bone indices |
| ---: | --- | ---: | --- |
| 61 | `左腕袖IK` | 58 | 57 |
| 62 | `左手袖IK` | 59 | 58 |
| 63 | `左手首袖IK` | 60 | 59 |
| 95 | `右腕袖IK` | 92 | 91 |
| 96 | `右手袖IK` | 93 | 92 |
| 97 | `右手首袖IK` | 94 | 93 |

But Uka's **only two bone append/grant records** are **`左目` (index 34) and `右目` (index 36)**, both rotation grants sourced from eye parent index 32. Thus the sleeve problem is **not explained by the existing bone grants**; missing sleeve IK is a more direct hypothesis.

[Current public-motion docs](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/docs/public-motion.md) and [`examples/main.ts`](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/examples/main.ts#L156-L179) explicitly run the left direct PMX as raw `AnimationMixer` only (no `MMDAnimationHelper`, IK, grant controller or physics). Both right glTF assets are converted with `solver:'none', physics:'none'` and use retained `VMDPlayer.seek` without IK. Therefore BOTH sides intentionally omit those sleeve IK chains.

This makes missing sleeve IK a **testable leading hypothesis, not yet proof of the visual cause**. Also inspect sleeve bone parent hierarchy, vertex skin weights, animated VMD arm/sleeve tracks and whether physics-dependent bones are involved; do not claim original MMD parity without reference measurements.

Note: [`solverDiagnostics`](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/packages/mmd-solver/index.ts#L512-L533) currently reports `fixed-axis` execution as unsupported for solver v3; Uka has **four fixed-axis bones**. Do not simply toggle full IK on only one side and declare comparison correct. Diagnose actual relevant dependencies; a compatible sleeve-only solver path may require further work.

## Requested implementation

### A. One model / one glTF with named animation choices

- [ ] Generate **one logical glTF asset per character** (Uka one `.gltf` with its shared external buffers/images; Gene Light one `.glb` or `.gltf`, whichever meets size/performance needs) containing **three distinctly named/identifiable animations**: Uka `04_littlesmile` + `02_laugh` + Uka `22_apology`; Gene `01_happy` + `02_laugh` + Gene `22_apology`. Keep the existing Rest/manual mode as a non-clip base-pose state. **Do not duplicate the model nodes, skin, geometry, textures, or independent scenes for each motion within the asset.**
- [ ] Retain each exact VMD's binary `source` inside its **own** `MMD_animation_vmd` v6 payload with correct channel ownership, per-animation rest/targets, track metadata and diagnostics. Keep existing source pins, SHA-256 checks, attribution, Gene usage restrictions, source-model comments, and full downloadable glTF compatibility. Validate a normal GLTFLoader's core fallback behavior independently from exact extension playback; no double playback.
- [ ] Extend the existing converter/build path to add multiple VMD animations to the **same converted Document / same shared skeleton**, using common bone/morph identities. Consider a reusable `vmds`/motion-list API or equivalent documented tool; retain current single-VMD API semantics and tests. Avoid merging multiple independently converted full scenes or copying VMD payloads without validating node indices, rest, morph channels, accessor buffers and extension schema.
- [ ] Ensure the built `animations[]` entries have stable IDs/names. Loading both Toon and PBR glTF instances must expose all matching `VMDPlayer`s and allow unambiguous Motion-select mapping independent of array reordering. Safely handle the fact that multiple players share **one root** and motion ownership: exactly one active player per glTF instance, and previous weights/rest/pose must be completely reset when changing clips, including backwards seek or switching to Rest.
- [ ] Load each character **once**, then switch only the left `AnimationMixer` action and the active right VMD player (one per Toon/PBR scene), with a single absolute shared clock. The left PMX animation clips may be created/cached from the original VMD bytes once at initialization. Ensure clip changes do **not** call `dispose()`, recreate the WebGPU renderer, reload PMX/glTF/assets, reinstall plugins, reset orbit/camera, or create a second canvas. A new model choice (Uka ↔ Gene) *may* still rebuild the character and resources.
- [ ] Update `examples/demo.ts` / `examples/main.ts` so switching Rest ↔ facial sample ↔ Laugh ↔ Apology only swaps animation state, preserving camera, Toon/PBR, Outline, motion selection and controls. Keep reliable pause/play, restart, loop, reverse seek, variable clip duration, end-of-clip behavior, hidden page/BFCache, source errors/retry and model changes. All controls disabled only when a genuine failure/loading state requires it.
- [ ] The public preview currently projects GPU morph buffers using only the **selected** clip's active vertex targets. With one model loaded for many motions, compute a safe **union of all motion-active targets plus manual Uka expressions**, or another proven incremental GPU buffer strategy that does not re-create the model, silently drop a target, or invalidate Three.js compiled morph layouts. Measure/limit GPU and network costs; preserve complete CPU metadata and downloadable targets.
- [ ] Remove redundant old motion-specific `.gltf` **model** outputs from the published path if compatibility allows, or document their retention as legacy downloads. The **visible demo** must not depend on these as separate models. Keep source VMDs pinned and cached.

### B. Model selector copy

- [ ] In [`examples/index.html`](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/examples/index.html), change just the user-facing `#demo-model` option labels from **`Uka comparison` → `Uka`** and **`Gene Light comparison` → `Gene Light`**. Preserve option `value=\"uka\"`/`value=\"gene\"`, model routing, existing `MMD`/`glTF` pane headings, accessibility/ARIA roles and collapsible source credits.
- [ ] Update tests that asserted the old visible option labels. Do not add more explanatory prose around the canvas or rename the model itself.

### C. Determine and correct Uka sleeve follow

- [ ] Reproduce the visually detached sleeves on **Uka `02_laugh` and `22_apology`**, in both PMX and glTF panes, at recorded VMD frames. Capture front/side views and arm/sleeve joint transforms; include **which sleeve mesh vertices are weighted to which source bones**, their parent chains, PMX fixed-axis flags, and any physics dependencies. Use actual Uka source rather than synthetic-only evidence.
- [ ] Run **controlled A/B variants**: current raw mixer without IK/grants/physics; direct PMX with the **six named sleeve IK chains** enabled (physics disabled, other IK controllers constrained/off); optionally a diagnostic reference with full library PMX helper if necessary. Determine if sleeve IK alone restores follow and document mismatches, required evaluation order and effect on arm trajectories.
- [ ] Separate the role of **eye-only grants**, sleeve IK, ordinary hierarchy/skinning and physics (Uka contains 164 rigid bodies/151 joints). If real cause is instead a missing bone animation mapping or a skinning/weight bug, identify and fix that **on both sides**, with measured evidence. Never use a one-off vertex/bone copy hack to mask the symptom.
- [ ] For the glTF path, inspect possible supported isolated sleeve IK execution from the retained PMX/solver metadata and current runtime. The right-hand `MMD_skeleton_solver` v3 may retain more than the current executor supports (notably fixed axes); any new execution must preserve valid source, shared timing and original bone behavior and be diagnosed explicitly. Do **not** enable a non-equivalent solver on one side while claiming exact comparison.
- [ ] Implement the minimum **symmetric** sleeve-follow correction supported by the findings, preferably as a separately controllable/diagnosed sleeve IK mode with **physics still OFF**. If equivalence or runtime support is blocked, clearly report the blocker and scope a follow-up issue; don't claim the sleeves are fixed on a code path that still drops required IK. Do not silently enable unrelated foot IK or all physics; update scope/credits to say truthfully whether sleeve IK is used.
- [ ] Preserve the independent MMD vs glTF motion comparison and existing constrained animations. Check that eye grants, non-vertex morph omissions and changing skeletal pose results are not misrepresented.

## Verification and acceptance

- [ ] **Network and lifecycle:** After first Uka/Gene load, switching among all four Motion dropdown values creates **no new model/skin/texture/glTF fetch**, no second canvas, no new WebGPU renderer or entire scene disposal. Only motion actions/players change. Record request counts and render/pose stability; measure time/memory before/after.
- [ ] **Single asset:** Inspect downloaded glTF/glb: exactly **one character skeleton/scene** and **three separate named VMD extension animations** with original retained bytes. Node and browser tests check shared rest/bind semantics, GLB/glTF reload, core fallback access, no extension ownership collisions and stable mapping of each animation to its source hash.
- [ ] **Playback:** For both Uka and Gene, exercise facial sample → Laugh → Apology → facial sample → Rest and Uka↔Gene; test 0, nonzero and terminal frames, backward seek, play/pause, restart, looping, Toon/PBR and Outline. Compare time, mapped bone matrices and active morphs on each side, showing full pose reset and no accidental mixing of old and new animation channels.
- [ ] **Sleeves:** Add real-Uka regression evidence demonstrating whether the six sleeve IK chains explain the detached sleeve observation, including quantified shoulder/arm/sleeve world transforms and rendered sleeve position at changing frames. If fixed, show both panes following with no unintended full-physics or foot-IK execution. If blocked, surface an explicit limitation and test the diagnostic instead of asserting a fix.
- [ ] **UI:** Model selector shows **`Uka`** and **`Gene Light`** exactly, not `comparison`; retain layout, desktop/mobile 390px behavior, source attribution and no verbose always-visible copy.
- [ ] No unacknowledged regressions to the synthetic conformance suite, material/shadow/outline rendering, original pinned assets, hash verification, error/Retry, navigation and page suspension.
- [ ] Run `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, relevant real-asset `npm run test:browser`, `npm run check:links`, `git diff --check`. Report actual failures/skips and any unsupported MMD-original equivalence. CI success alone does not establish sleeve fidelity.

## Useful references

- [Issue #65 / PR #66: body motions](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/issues/65)
- [Issue #63 / PR #64: synchronized base comparison](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/issues/63)
- [Public motion documentation](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/docs/public-motion.md)
- [Uka PMX IK/grant inventory](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/docs/uka-inventory.json)
- [Current glTF VMD importer/player](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/packages/three-mmd-vmd/index.ts)
- [Current source transport and solver capability constraints](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/docs/source-transport.md)
- [Direct PMX reference MMDAnimationHelper](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader/blob/main/src/animation/MMDAnimationHelper.ts)

## Optional validation

Visual side-by-side comparison with Uka's `02_laugh` and `22_apology` using front/side viewpoints before and after sleeve-IK correction. Original Windows MMD parity is optional research, not an unsupported acceptance claim.

## Required post-merge verification

None required unless deployment behavior changes; any live Pages checks should be recorded with actual revision and URL.
